cases.name: open-palette-from-any-overlay-state
cases.condition: The open-palette command is invoked; it unconditionally sets the overlay to 'palette', regardless of the overlay's prior state.
cases.outcome: It sets the overlay to 'palette' regardless of its prior state.
cases.domain: any prior overlay state

cases.name: open-help-from-any-overlay-state
cases.condition: The open-help command is invoked; it unconditionally sets the overlay to 'help', regardless of the overlay's prior state.
cases.outcome: It sets the overlay to 'help' regardless of its prior state.
cases.domain: any prior overlay state

cases.name: escape-with-overlay-open
cases.condition: The escape command is invoked while ui.overlay() is not undefined; it sets the overlay to undefined, returns immediately, and leaves the selection unchanged.
cases.outcome: It sets the overlay to undefined, returns immediately, and leaves the selection unchanged.
cases.domain: any defined overlay value and any selection state

cases.name: escape-without-overlay
cases.condition: The escape command is invoked while ui.overlay() is undefined; it clears the selection.
cases.outcome: It clears the selection.
cases.domain: any selection state

cases.name: no-editor-state
cases.condition: The editor state is null, so App renders the start screen instead of the editor shell.
cases.outcome: It renders the start screen instead of the editor shell.

cases.name: editor-state-ready
cases.condition: The editor state is non-null, so App renders the editor shell with IslandFrame and its canvas, toolbar, and inspector content.
cases.outcome: It renders the editor shell with IslandFrame containing the canvas, toolbar, and inspector.

cases.name: no-overlay-open
cases.condition: The UI overlay signal is undefined, so neither overlay surface is mounted.
cases.outcome: It mounts neither the palette nor the help overlay.

cases.name: palette-overlay-open
cases.condition: The UI overlay identifies the palette, so the palette is mounted as a sibling of IslandFrame and its rows are built for that opening.
cases.outcome: It mounts the palette as an IslandFrame sibling and builds its rows for that opening.

cases.name: help-overlay-open
cases.condition: The UI overlay identifies help, so the help sheet is mounted as a sibling of IslandFrame using COMMANDS and KEYMAP directly.
cases.outcome: It mounts the help sheet as an IslandFrame sibling using COMMANDS and KEYMAP directly.

cases.name: palette-reopened
cases.condition: The palette is opened again after a previous opening, so its surface and query state start fresh rather than retaining the previous query.
cases.outcome: It remounts the palette so its surface and query state start fresh.

cases.name: palette-without-geometry
cases.condition: The palette is open but no scene geometry has been published, so it still opens with command rows and has no element rows.
cases.outcome: It opens the palette with command rows only and no element rows.

cases.name: palette-with-geometry
cases.condition: The palette is open and current scene geometry is available, so command rows are concatenated before element rows generated from the diagram geometry.
cases.outcome: It concatenates command rows before element rows generated from the diagram geometry.

cases.name: excluded-palette-commands
cases.condition: Palette rows are generated, and commands excluded by PALETTE_EXCLUDED, including open-palette and open-help, are absent; no listed action reopens an overlay.
cases.outcome: It omits PALETTE_EXCLUDED commands, including open-palette and open-help, so no listed action reopens an overlay.
cases.domain: the excluded overlay-opening commands

cases.name: palette-close
cases.condition: The palette invokes onClose, which clears the overlay signal by setting it to undefined.
cases.outcome: It clears the overlay signal by setting it to undefined.

cases.name: choose-command-with-context
cases.condition: A palette command action is chosen while a command-context accessor exists; App closes the overlay first and dispatches the command through onCommand.
cases.outcome: It closes the overlay first, then dispatches the command through onCommand.
cases.domain: any non-excluded PaletteAction command

cases.name: choose-command-without-context
cases.condition: A palette command action is chosen while no command-context accessor exists; App closes the overlay first and onCommand performs no dispatch.
cases.outcome: It closes the overlay first, then onCommand performs no dispatch.
cases.domain: any non-excluded PaletteAction command

cases.name: choose-element-with-matching-entry
cases.condition: A palette element action is chosen, its ref is selected as the sole selection, and elementKey(ref) finds an entry in the current scene geometry byKey index; when a command context exists, the viewport is then centered on that entry's bounds within the context rect.
cases.outcome: It closes first, selects exactly the ref, and centers the viewport on the matched bounds within the context rect.
cases.domain: one of the four element-reference kinds with a matching geometry entry

cases.name: choose-element-without-entry
cases.condition: A palette element action is chosen and its ref has no entry in the current scene geometry byKey index; the ref is selected as the sole selection and the viewport is left unchanged.
cases.outcome: It closes first and selects exactly the ref without changing the viewport.
cases.domain: one of the four element-reference kinds absent from byKey

cases.name: choose-element-without-context
cases.condition: A palette element action is chosen and geometry contains a matching entry, but no command-context accessor exists; the ref is selected as the sole selection and no viewport pan is performed.
cases.outcome: It closes first and selects exactly the ref without panning the viewport.
cases.domain: one of the four element-reference kinds with a matching entry

cases.name: element-key-disambiguates-reference
cases.condition: A chosen element ref is looked up with elementKey(ref), so a node and a group sharing the same bare id are distinguished by their keyed references rather than colliding in byKey.
cases.outcome: It uses elementKey(ref) to distinguish same-id nodes and groups in byKey.
cases.domain: references whose bare ids may be shared across element kinds

cases.name: close-before-command
cases.condition: A palette command action is chosen; clearing the overlay precedes command dispatch so commands such as focus-inspector retain their focus movement after the palette unmounts.
cases.outcome: It clears the overlay before dispatch so focus movement from commands such as focus-inspector is preserved.
cases.domain: any palette command, especially focus-inspector

cases.name: close-before-element-action
cases.condition: A palette element action is chosen; clearing the overlay precedes selection and any viewport centering.
cases.outcome: It clears the overlay before selecting the element and centering the viewport.

cases.name: apple-no-modifiers
cases.condition: navigator.platform contains 'Mac'; the chord has neither the meta modifier nor the shift modifier. The key is displayed without a modifier prefix and is formatted according to the key rules.
cases.outcome: On a Mac, it returns the formatted key alone with no modifier prefix when neither meta nor shift is active.
cases.domain: any supported Chord key

cases.name: apple-meta-only
cases.condition: navigator.platform contains 'Mac'; the chord has the meta modifier but not shift. The display starts with U+2318 immediately followed by the formatted key.
cases.outcome: On a Mac, it prefixes the formatted key immediately with U+2318 when only meta is active.
cases.domain: any supported Chord key

cases.name: apple-shift-only
cases.condition: navigator.platform contains 'Mac'; the chord has shift but not the meta modifier. The display starts with U+21E7 immediately followed by the formatted key.
cases.outcome: On a Mac, it prefixes the formatted key immediately with U+21E7 when only shift is active.
cases.domain: any supported Chord key

cases.name: apple-meta-and-shift
cases.condition: navigator.platform contains 'Mac'; the chord has both meta and shift. The display is U+2318 followed immediately by U+21E7 and then the formatted key, with no separators.
cases.outcome: On a Mac, it returns U+2318 followed immediately by U+21E7 and the formatted key, with no separators.
cases.domain: any supported Chord key

cases.name: non-apple-no-modifiers
cases.condition: navigator.platform does not contain 'Mac'; the chord has neither the meta modifier nor the shift modifier. The key is displayed without a modifier prefix and is formatted according to the key rules.
cases.outcome: Off Apple platforms, it returns the formatted key alone with no modifier prefix when neither meta nor shift is active.
cases.domain: any supported Chord key

cases.name: non-apple-meta-only
cases.condition: navigator.platform does not contain 'Mac'; the chord has the meta modifier but not shift. Because this modifier is represented as Ctrl off Apple, the display is 'Ctrl+' followed by the formatted key.
cases.outcome: Off Apple platforms, it prefixes the formatted key with Ctrl+ when only meta is active.
cases.domain: any supported Chord key

cases.name: non-apple-shift-only
cases.condition: navigator.platform does not contain 'Mac'; the chord has shift but not the meta modifier. The display is 'Shift+' followed by the formatted key.
cases.outcome: Off Apple platforms, it prefixes the formatted key with Shift+ when only shift is active.
cases.domain: any supported Chord key

cases.name: non-apple-meta-and-shift
cases.condition: navigator.platform does not contain 'Mac'; the chord has both meta and shift. The display is 'Ctrl+Shift+' followed by the formatted key.
cases.outcome: Off Apple platforms, it prefixes the formatted key with Ctrl+Shift+ when both meta and shift are active.
cases.domain: any supported Chord key

cases.name: single-character-key
cases.condition: The key is a single character; it is upper-cased, while any applicable platform-specific modifier composition is applied before it.
cases.outcome: It upper-cases a single-character key after applying any applicable platform-specific modifier composition.
cases.domain: any single-character KeyboardEvent.key value

cases.name: question-mark-key
cases.condition: The key is the single character '?'; upper-casing leaves it as '?', while any applicable modifier composition is applied before it.
cases.outcome: It leaves the single-character key ? unchanged after applying any applicable modifier composition.

cases.name: arrow-up-key
cases.condition: The key is exactly 'ArrowUp'; it is renamed to 'Up', while any applicable modifier composition is applied before it.
cases.outcome: It renames ArrowUp to Up after applying any applicable modifier composition.

cases.name: arrow-down-key
cases.condition: The key is exactly 'ArrowDown'; it is renamed to 'Down', while any applicable modifier composition is applied before it.
cases.outcome: It renames ArrowDown to Down after applying any applicable modifier composition.

cases.name: arrow-left-key
cases.condition: The key is exactly 'ArrowLeft'; it is renamed to 'Left', while any applicable modifier composition is applied before it.
cases.outcome: It renames ArrowLeft to Left after applying any applicable modifier composition.

cases.name: arrow-right-key
cases.condition: The key is exactly 'ArrowRight'; it is renamed to 'Right', while any applicable modifier composition is applied before it.
cases.outcome: It renames ArrowRight to Right after applying any applicable modifier composition.

cases.name: escape-key
cases.condition: The key is exactly 'Escape'; it is renamed to 'Esc', while any applicable modifier composition is applied before it.
cases.outcome: It renames Escape to Esc after applying any applicable modifier composition.

cases.name: other-multicharacter-key
cases.condition: The key has multiple characters and is not one of ArrowUp, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, or Escape; it is passed through verbatim, while any applicable modifier composition is applied before it.
cases.outcome: It passes through any other multi-character key verbatim after applying any applicable modifier composition.
cases.domain: any other multi-character KeyboardEvent.key value

cases.name: backspace-key
cases.condition: The key is exactly 'Backspace'; it remains 'Backspace' and is not renamed to 'Delete', while any applicable modifier composition is applied before it.
cases.outcome: It preserves Backspace as Backspace rather than renaming it to Delete, after applying any applicable modifier composition.

cases.name: delete-key
cases.condition: The key is exactly 'Delete'; it remains 'Delete', while any applicable modifier composition is applied before it.
cases.outcome: It preserves Delete as Delete after applying any applicable modifier composition.

cases.name: enter-key
cases.condition: The key is exactly 'Enter'; it remains 'Enter', while any applicable modifier composition is applied before it.
cases.outcome: It preserves Enter as Enter after applying any applicable modifier composition.

cases.name: platform-read-per-call
cases.condition: The function is called after navigator.platform has changed between calls; each call uses the current platform value, so a value containing 'Mac' selects Apple symbols and a value not containing 'Mac' selects Ctrl/Shift words.
cases.outcome: It reads the current navigator.platform on every call, selecting Apple symbols when it contains Mac and Ctrl/Shift words otherwise.
cases.domain: any sequence of calls with differing navigator.platform values

cases.name: user-agent-ignored
cases.condition: The user agent indicates an Apple or non-Apple device independently of navigator.platform; only whether navigator.platform contains 'Mac' affects the result.
cases.outcome: It ignores the user agent and selects the output solely from whether navigator.platform contains Mac.
cases.domain: any userAgent value

cases.name: mount-focuses-input
cases.condition: The palette is mounted by its caller while open; the text input receives focus immediately on mount.
cases.outcome: Focuses the text input immediately when the palette mounts.

cases.name: query-produces-filtered-rows
cases.condition: The query filters the available palette items to one or more rows; the filtered rows render with each label on the left and detail dimmed on the right.
cases.outcome: Filters the available items and renders each matching row with its label on the left and dimmed detail on the right.
cases.domain: any query producing a non-empty filtered list

cases.name: query-produces-no-rows
cases.condition: The query filters the available palette items to an empty list; no result rows are available for selection.
cases.outcome: Renders no selectable result rows when the filtered list is empty.
cases.domain: any query producing an empty filtered list

cases.name: query-change-resets-highlight
cases.condition: The query changes, causing the filtered list to be recomputed; the highlighted index resets to 0 rather than being retained.
cases.outcome: Resets the highlighted index to 0 whenever the query changes.
cases.domain: any query change

cases.name: arrow-down-advances-highlight
cases.condition: ArrowDown is pressed on the input while the filtered list has multiple rows and the highlighted index is not the last index; the highlight advances by one and the event is prevented.
cases.outcome: Advances the highlight by one and prevents the default event.
cases.domain: a filtered list with at least two rows and an index below its last index

cases.name: arrow-down-clamps-at-last-row
cases.condition: ArrowDown is pressed on the input while the highlight is already on the last filtered row; the highlight remains on that row and the event is prevented.
cases.outcome: Keeps the highlight on the last row and prevents the default event.
cases.domain: any non-empty filtered list with the highlight at its last index

cases.name: arrow-up-retreats-highlight
cases.condition: ArrowUp is pressed on the input while the highlighted index is greater than 0; the highlight moves back by one and the event is prevented.
cases.outcome: Moves the highlight back by one and prevents the default event.
cases.domain: a filtered list with a highlight index from 1 through the last index

cases.name: arrow-up-clamps-at-first-row
cases.condition: ArrowUp is pressed on the input while the highlight is at index 0; the highlight remains at index 0 and the event is prevented.
cases.outcome: Keeps the highlight at index 0 and prevents the default event.
cases.domain: any filtered list with the highlight at index 0

cases.name: enter-chooses-highlighted-row
cases.condition: Enter is pressed on the input while the filtered list is non-empty; onChoose is called with the action of the highlighted row and the event is prevented.
cases.outcome: Calls onChoose with the highlighted row’s action and prevents the default event.
cases.domain: any non-empty filtered list

cases.name: enter-on-empty-list-does-nothing
cases.condition: Enter is pressed on the input while the filtered list is empty; no row action is chosen and no close callback is invoked.
cases.outcome: Does nothing, including not choosing an action or calling onClose.

cases.name: escape-closes-palette
cases.condition: Escape is pressed on the input; onClose is called.
cases.outcome: Calls onClose when Escape is pressed.

cases.name: row-click-chooses-row
cases.condition: A filtered result row is clicked; onChoose is called with that row's action, equivalent to choosing it with Enter.
cases.outcome: Calls onChoose with the clicked row’s action.
cases.domain: any rendered result row

cases.name: scrim-click-closes-palette
cases.condition: The scrim itself is clicked; onClose is called.
cases.outcome: Calls onClose when the scrim itself is clicked.

cases.name: scrim-blocks-background-pointer
cases.condition: A pointer event occurs behind the palette on the scrim; the event is swallowed so it does not reach the canvas or move a selection.
cases.outcome: Swallows pointer events on the scrim so they cannot reach the canvas or move a selection.
cases.domain: any pointer event targeting the scrim/background outside the palette

cases.name: input-key-does-not-reach-global-handler
cases.condition: A handled key originates in the palette's text input; the global keyboard command handler ignores it because the target is an input element.
cases.outcome: The global keyboard handler ignores the key because its target is an input element.
cases.domain: any key event originating in the palette input

cases.name: ordered-keymap-entries
cases.condition: The keymap prop contains entries whose commands are present in commands; one row is rendered for each entry in the prop's original order, using formatChord for the chord and the matching command label.
cases.outcome: Renders one row per matching keymap entry in the prop's original order, formatting each chord with formatChord and showing its command label.
cases.domain: any ordered keymap with commands present in the commands prop

cases.name: empty-keymap
cases.condition: The keymap prop has no entries, so the sheet renders no command rows.
cases.outcome: Renders no command rows when the keymap prop is empty.

cases.name: missing-command-skipped
cases.condition: A keymap entry names a command absent from the commands prop; that entry is skipped rather than rendered with its raw command id.
cases.outcome: Skips any keymap entry whose command is absent from the commands prop.
cases.domain: any keymap entry whose command id is absent from commands

cases.name: multiple-chords-per-command
cases.condition: Several keymap entries name the same command; every entry produces its own row rather than being collapsed to one chord.
cases.outcome: Renders a separate row for every keymap entry even when several entries name the same command.
cases.domain: any number of entries sharing a command

cases.name: backspace-and-delete-chords
cases.condition: A command is bound to both Backspace and Delete; both distinct chord rows are rendered, with the names passed through verbatim by formatChord.
cases.outcome: Renders distinct rows for both Backspace and Delete, passing both names verbatim through formatChord.

cases.name: mount-focuses-root
cases.condition: The sheet is mounted; its root has tabIndex={-1} and is focused so the sheet can receive keyboard events and its own Escape handler can run.
cases.outcome: On mount, gives the root tabIndex={-1} and focuses it so it receives keyboard events and its Escape handler can run.

cases.name: escape-dismissal
cases.condition: The focused sheet root receives an Escape key event; onClose is called.
cases.outcome: Calls onClose when the focused sheet root receives an Escape key event.

cases.name: scrim-click-dismissal
cases.condition: The scrim is clicked; onClose is called.
cases.outcome: Calls onClose when the scrim is clicked.

cases.name: opened-without-mouse
cases.condition: A user opens the sheet without using a mouse; focus on the root permits keyboard dismissal through Escape.
cases.outcome: Focuses the root so a sheet opened without a mouse can be dismissed with Escape from the keyboard.

cases.name: closed-sheet-not-rendered
cases.condition: The sheet is not open because its caller has not mounted it under Show; no sheet UI is rendered.
cases.outcome: Renders no sheet UI when the caller does not mount the closed sheet under Show.

cases.name: no-text-input
cases.condition: The sheet receives no text input; it has no text-entry behavior.
cases.outcome: Provides no text-entry behavior or text input handling.

cases.name: no-highlighted-row
cases.condition: The sheet has no highlighted-row state or row-selection behavior.
cases.outcome: Provides no highlighted-row state or row-selection behavior.

cases.name: has-declared-value
cases.condition: The exported ReadonlySet contains exactly the nine excluded CommandId members: 'escape', 'nudge-up', 'nudge-down', 'nudge-left', 'nudge-right', 'ring-next', 'ring-prev', 'open-palette', and 'open-help'.
cases.outcome: Exports a ReadonlySet containing exactly the nine specified CommandId members: escape, the four nudge commands, the two ring commands, open-palette, and open-help.

cases.name: empty-commands
cases.condition: The commands argument is empty; no palette rows are produced regardless of keymap contents.
cases.outcome: Returns no palette rows when the commands argument is empty, regardless of keymap contents.

cases.name: included-command
cases.condition: A command entry whose id is not in PALETTE_EXCLUDED produces one row with its Command.label, key equal to 'command:' followed by its id, and detail derived from the keymap argument.
cases.outcome: Creates one row for each non-excluded command using its label, a key of 'command:' plus its id, and detail derived from the supplied keymap.
cases.domain: any non-excluded command entry

cases.name: preserved-command-order
cases.condition: Multiple non-excluded command entries are supplied; output rows follow the commands argument order rather than registry order.
cases.outcome: Returns multiple non-excluded rows in the order of the commands argument.
cases.domain: any non-empty ordered list of non-excluded command entries

cases.name: excluded-command
cases.condition: A command entry whose id is in PALETTE_EXCLUDED is skipped and produces no row.
cases.outcome: Skips any command whose id is in PALETTE_EXCLUDED.
cases.domain: any excluded command id

cases.name: mixed-excluded-and-included
cases.condition: The commands argument mixes excluded and non-excluded entries; excluded entries are omitted while included entries retain their relative input order.
cases.outcome: Omits excluded commands while preserving the relative input order of included commands.
cases.domain: any mixture of excluded and non-excluded entries

cases.name: matching-chord
cases.condition: The keymap argument contains an entry whose command matches an included command id; that entry is rendered with formatChord and placed in the row detail.
cases.outcome: Uses the first matching keymap entry, rendered with formatChord, as the included command's detail.
cases.domain: any matching keymap entry

cases.name: missing-chord
cases.condition: An included command has no matching keymap entry; its row detail is the empty string.
cases.outcome: Sets detail to the empty string when an included command has no matching keymap entry.
cases.domain: any included command with no matching keymap entry

cases.name: first-chord-wins
cases.condition: More than one keymap entry matches an included command id; only the first matching entry in keymap order is rendered, and later matching chords are not shown.
cases.outcome: Renders only the first matching keymap chord and ignores later matches.
cases.domain: any ordered set of two or more matching keymap entries

cases.name: unrelated-keymap-entries
cases.condition: The keymap contains entries for other command ids; those entries do not affect the detail of an included command.
cases.outcome: Ignores keymap entries whose command ids do not match the included command.
cases.domain: any number of non-matching keymap entries

cases.name: argument-registries-used
cases.condition: Commands and keymap fixture arguments differ from any module-level registries; rows are still built from the supplied arguments, including their supplied labels and chords.
cases.outcome: Builds rows from the supplied command and keymap arguments, including their labels and chords, rather than module-level registries.
cases.domain: any fixture command and keymap arrays

cases.name: empty-diagram
cases.condition: The diagram has no nodes, groups, annotations, or edges; the function returns an empty array.
cases.outcome: Returns an empty array when the diagram contains no nodes, groups, annotations, or edges.

cases.name: labeled-node-or-group
cases.condition: A node or group has a label list whose index-0 Localization source is non-empty after trimming; one row is produced with its element key, that source as label, and the corresponding kind as detail.
cases.outcome: Produces one row for the node or group using its element key, trimmed index-0 label source, and corresponding kind as detail.
cases.domain: one of: node, group

cases.name: labeled-annotation
cases.condition: An annotation has a content list whose index-0 Localization source is non-empty after trimming; one row is produced with its element key, that source as label, and annotation as detail.
cases.outcome: Produces one row for the annotation using its element key, trimmed index-0 content source as label, and annotation as detail.
cases.domain: any annotation with non-empty trimmed index-0 content source

cases.name: empty-label-list-fallback
cases.condition: A node or group has an empty label list, so its row label falls back to the element id.
cases.outcome: Produces the node or group row with its element id as the label when the label list is empty.
cases.domain: one of: node, group

cases.name: empty-content-list-fallback
cases.condition: An annotation has an empty content list, so its row label falls back to the element id.
cases.outcome: Produces the annotation row with its element id as the label when the content list is empty.
cases.domain: any annotation with no content entries

cases.name: blank-index-zero-source-fallback
cases.condition: A node, group, or annotation has an index-0 label/content Localization whose source is empty after trimming; its row label falls back to the element id.
cases.outcome: Produces the row with its element id as the label when the index-0 label or content source is blank after trimming.
cases.domain: one of: node, group, annotation

cases.name: edges-excluded
cases.condition: The diagram contains edges; edges produce no palette rows because they are not represented in the scene index bounds.
cases.outcome: Omits edges entirely because they have no scene-index bounds for panning.
cases.domain: any collection of edges

cases.name: mixed-element-collections
cases.condition: The diagram contains any combination of nodes, groups, annotations, and edges; rows are produced only for nodes, groups, and annotations, with no row for any edge.
cases.outcome: Produces rows only for nodes, groups, and annotations, omitting every edge.
cases.domain: any combination of node, group, annotation, and edge

cases.name: key-sorted-results
cases.condition: The diagram contains multiple row-producing elements; all produced rows are sorted by elementKey(ref) ascending before being returned, independently of record insertion order.
cases.outcome: Returns all produced rows sorted ascending by elementKey(ref), regardless of record insertion order.
cases.domain: two or more nodes, groups, or annotations with distinct keys

cases.name: integer-like-id-ordering
cases.condition: Row-producing elements have integer-like ids whose record enumeration order may differ from insertion order; the returned rows still follow ascending element keys.
cases.outcome: Returns rows with integer-like ids in ascending element-key order, independent of record enumeration order.
cases.domain: two or more row-producing elements with integer-like ids

cases.name: empty-items
cases.condition: The items array is empty; the result is empty for any query.
cases.outcome: Returns an empty array for every query when the items array is empty.
cases.domain: any query string

cases.name: blank-query
cases.condition: The query is empty or consists only of whitespace after trimming; every item is returned in the original input order.
cases.outcome: Returns every item in its original input order when the trimmed query is blank.
cases.domain: empty or whitespace-only strings

cases.name: trimmed-query
cases.condition: Leading or trailing whitespace is removed before matching, so surrounding spaces do not affect the result.
cases.outcome: Trims leading and trailing whitespace from the query before matching.
cases.domain: any query with leading or trailing whitespace

cases.name: case-insensitive-label-match
cases.condition: A non-blank query matches an item when its trimmed text occurs as a case-insensitive substring of the item's label.
cases.outcome: For a non-blank query, returns items whose labels contain the trimmed query as a case-insensitive contiguous substring.
cases.domain: any non-blank string and labels containing it under case folding

cases.name: detail-does-not-match
cases.condition: Text present only in an item's detail does not make that item match; matching uses the label only.
cases.outcome: Ignores detail text entirely when determining whether an item matches.
cases.domain: any query occurring in detail but not in label

cases.name: starts-with-tier
cases.condition: Among matching items, labels that start with the trimmed query case-insensitively are ranked before labels that contain the query only later.
cases.outcome: Ranks matching items whose labels start with the trimmed query case-insensitively before other matching items.
cases.domain: any query with both prefix and non-prefix matches

cases.name: stable-prefix-order
cases.condition: Multiple matching items whose labels start with the query retain their original relative input order.
cases.outcome: Preserves input order among matching items whose labels start with the query.
cases.domain: two or more prefix-matching items

cases.name: stable-containing-order
cases.condition: Multiple matching items whose labels contain but do not start with the query retain their original relative input order.
cases.outcome: Preserves input order among matching items that contain but do not start with the query.
cases.domain: two or more non-prefix matching items

cases.name: mixed-tier-stable-ranking
cases.condition: The result places all prefix matches first and all other substring matches afterward, while preserving input order within each tier.
cases.outcome: Places all prefix matches before later substring matches while preserving input order within both tiers.
cases.domain: any input containing matches in both tiers

cases.name: no-match
cases.condition: A non-blank query that occurs in no label returns an empty result.
cases.outcome: Returns an empty array when a non-blank query occurs in no label.
cases.domain: any non-blank string absent from every label

cases.name: exact-label-match
cases.condition: A query equal to an entire label, ignoring case and trimmed surrounding whitespace, matches as a prefix-tier item.
cases.outcome: Treats a case-insensitive whole-label match after trimming as a prefix-tier match.
cases.domain: any label and case/whitespace variant of that label

cases.name: substring-not-subsequence
cases.condition: Matching requires contiguous substring occurrence; a query whose characters occur only as a non-contiguous subsequence does not match.
cases.outcome: Requires the query characters to occur contiguously, so a non-contiguous subsequence does not match.
cases.domain: any non-contiguous query such as 'nd' against 'node'

cases.name: case-insensitive-ranking
cases.condition: Prefix classification and substring matching are both case-insensitive.
cases.outcome: Performs both substring matching and prefix classification without regard to case.
cases.domain: any query and label differing only in letter case

cases.name: empty-query-order-preserved
cases.condition: For an empty or whitespace-only query, no ranking is applied and all items remain in input order, including duplicate or otherwise identical items.
cases.outcome: Returns all items unchanged in input order for an empty or whitespace-only query, including duplicates.
cases.domain: any items array with a blank query

cases.name: matching-items-only-ranking
cases.condition: Nonmatching items are omitted and do not participate in prefix-versus-containing ranking among the retained items.
cases.outcome: Omits nonmatching items and ranks only the retained matching items by prefix versus later substring.
cases.domain: any input containing matching and nonmatching items

cases.name: select-command-with-v-chord
cases.condition: The selected toolbar command is Select and its first matching KEYMAP entry has the single-character chord 'v'; the tooltip renders the label as 'Select (V)'.
cases.outcome: It uses the Select command label and formats the single-character chord as uppercase V, producing the tooltip 'Select (V)'.

cases.name: toolbar-command-with-h-chord
cases.condition: The selected toolbar command's first matching KEYMAP entry has the single-character chord 'h' with no modifier; formatChord upper-cases it in the tooltip.
cases.outcome: It uses the command label and formats the unmodified single-character chord h as uppercase H in the tooltip.
cases.domain: any toolbar command bound first to the unmodified h chord

cases.name: toolbar-command-with-t-chord
cases.condition: The selected toolbar command's first matching KEYMAP entry has the single-character chord 't' with no modifier; formatChord upper-cases it in the tooltip.
cases.outcome: It uses the command label and formats the unmodified single-character chord t as uppercase T in the tooltip.
cases.domain: any toolbar command bound first to the unmodified t chord

cases.name: toolbar-command-with-n-chord
cases.condition: The selected toolbar command's first matching KEYMAP entry has the single-character chord 'n' with no modifier; formatChord upper-cases it in the tooltip.
cases.outcome: It uses the command label and formats the unmodified single-character chord n as uppercase N in the tooltip.
cases.domain: any toolbar command bound first to the unmodified n chord

cases.name: matching-keymap-entry
cases.condition: The command ID has one or more matching KEYMAP entries; the first matching entry is found, and the result is the command label followed by the first entry's formatted chord in parentheses.
cases.outcome: Returns the command label followed by the first matching entry's formatted chord in parentheses.
cases.domain: any command ID present in KEYMAP

cases.name: no-matching-keymap-entry
cases.condition: The command ID has no matching KEYMAP entry; the result is only the command label.
cases.outcome: Returns only the command label.
cases.domain: any command ID absent from KEYMAP

cases.name: meta-k-opens-palette
cases.condition: The keymap contains an entry mapping the chord key 'k' with meta true to the 'open-palette' command.
cases.outcome: The function should include a keymap entry mapping meta+K to the open-palette command.

cases.name: shift-question-opens-help
cases.condition: The keymap contains an entry mapping the chord key '?' with shift true to the 'open-help' command; the shift modifier is required for the chord to match the US-layout question-mark key event.
cases.outcome: The function should include a keymap entry mapping Shift+? to the open-help command, with shift required for matching the US-layout question-mark event.

cases.name: initial-overlay-undefined
cases.condition: Calling createUiState initializes the overlay signal to undefined and returns both the overlay signal and its setter on the UI state handle.
cases.outcome: Calling createUiState initializes the overlay signal to undefined and returns both the overlay signal and its setter on the UI state handle.

cases.name: positive-container-dimensions
cases.condition: The container has nonzero width and height; the function pans so the scaled centre of bounds coincides with the centre of the container in its own coordinates, while preserving the incoming zoom.
cases.outcome: Returns the viewport with its zoom preserved and pan adjusted so the scaled bounds centre coincides with the container's own-coordinate centre.
cases.domain: any viewport, bounds, and container rectangle with nonzero width and height

cases.name: zero-container-width
cases.condition: The container width is zero, so the function returns the incoming viewport unchanged, including its pan and zoom.
cases.outcome: Returns the incoming viewport unchanged, including its pan and zoom.
cases.domain: any viewport, bounds, and container rectangle whose width is 0

cases.name: zero-container-height
cases.condition: The container height is zero, so the function returns the incoming viewport unchanged, including its pan and zoom.
cases.outcome: Returns the incoming viewport unchanged, including its pan and zoom.
cases.domain: any viewport, bounds, and container rectangle whose height is 0

cases.name: off-origin-container
cases.condition: The container rectangle has a nonzero page-position left or top; those page offsets are ignored, and centring uses only width and height in the container's own coordinates.
cases.outcome: Ignores the container's left and top offsets and centres using only its width and height in its own coordinates.
cases.domain: any nonzero left or top offsets with nonzero container width and height
